metadata.name: UnitContracts
metadata.description: Guides > Unit contracts. Dedicated page for `unitContracts` and `jsonui-test generate unit-stubs`, the third declaration surface after branchContracts and the test files. Eight sections: what the spec carries (the SET of cases, not the body, with the upstream measurement that decided that split), the declaration shape (target / cases / name / intent / optional platforms, unstated meaning every platform the project builds), what jui.config.json must supply (unitTestsDir per platform, testModule for iOS, testPackage for Android, and NOT CHECKED when a directory is undeclared), the generation contract (marker region, failing stubs, append-only and idempotent since jsonui-cli 1.8.48, nothing ever removed including undeclared cases and files whose markers the author deleted), the three drift kinds MISSING / UNDECLARED / NEVER RUNS with their denominators, the iOS test_ prefix and the two narrowings of the NEVER RUNS scan, the misspelled-key aggregate PROBLEM, and what a name-comparison cannot tell you. ~10-min read.

uiVariables.description: Three closing cards: branch contracts (the declaration side), branch tests (the other generator), testing (where unit tests sit in the whole test story).

notes: 2026-09-08 - Page created, requested 2026-09-07 and held until jsonui-cli 1.8.48 landed. The hold was deliberate: measuring 1.8.47 to write the generation section found that `generate unit-stubs` replaced the whole marker region with only the cases missing on that run, so hand-written bodies inside the markers were destroyed and consecutive runs oscillated with period two, meaning `--check` never reached 0. That was filed upstream and accepted for 1.8.48 with the append-based fix, and writing the section against 1.8.47 would have published a generation contract that stopped being true days later. Every claim on this page is measured on one fixture built for it — a config declaring all three faces with unitTestsDir plus testModule and testPackage, and one spec declaring five cases with one scoped to ios — run against the shipped 1.8.47 and 1.8.49 tag trees. The oscillation is stated from a probe that reproduces it rather than from the upstream report: the first attempt at that probe reported the two versions as AGREEING, because it generated the file fresh with every case already declared, so nothing was ever missing and the destructive path was never entered. Rebuilt in the order that reaches it — four cases generated, one body hand-written inside the markers, then a fifth case declared — 1.8.47 leaves one case in the file with the hand-written body gone, alternates between exactly two md5 values across five runs, and exits 1 from `--check` every time; 1.8.49 converges on run 1, keeps the hand-written body on all three faces, and runs 2-5 are byte-identical no-ops at exit 0. The NEVER RUNS narrowing for Swift local functions is measured the same way: one file with `func poll()` inside a test_-prefixed method draws one NEVER RUNS at 1.8.47 and none at 1.8.49. Section 8 states what the mechanism does not give, because the page otherwise reads as though a green `--check` were a statement about the tests rather than about their names.
